---
title: "Stage 6 – Regression on respondents"
case: trust
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at Part 3](../../slides/trust-one-day.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

This stage, about six hours of work, is the reproduction and the statistics behind it. The model that the original author (OA) fitted is a regression of distrust on concern with a long list of controls, fitted to respondents who are grouped in country-rounds and countries, and every one of those features is a decision with consequences: which controls to hold constant, whether the countries and rounds enter as fixed effects or as random intercepts, whether the respondents are weighted, and how the uncertainty is judged when a hundred thousand answers come from only sixteen countries. The module on statistical methods fits the same models to the country-year panel of the EU-frames case, which stage 10 builds. Read it with sixteen countries of respondents in mind in place of twenty-seven countries of years.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, Part 3, apart from the menu | The instruction of Task 2 of Multi100 read word for word and the aim of the reproduction; after the task, the file and the model, the two rebuilds of the data from the survey files and why they part ways over the vote controls; then the methods slides on comparisons within country-rounds, scales against their single items, survey weights and missing answers. The menu and Task 4 wait for stage 7. | 35 minutes |
| Task 3 in your report or working script | `fetch_multi100()` makes sure that the file of the analysts is in place, and the chunk of Task 3 fits the model of Table 3 of the paper without the unemployment rate, with random intercepts for countries and country-rounds, using `lme4::lmer()`. It gives *t* = 46.625 on 72,733 respondents, the value that Multi100 recorded for 6U3LL, and `prep/reproduce_6U3LL.R` holds the steps as a script. Then find out what the number depends on: the same specification gives 0.174 on 72,620 respondents of the course extract against 0.191 on the file of the analysts. The workspace reproduces this one analyst; the [case study](../../cases/trust/index.qmd#sec-reanalysts) sets out what the other four did, and the [exercise overview](../../cases/trust/exercise.qmd) adds N8P2J, the full model of Table 3, as an optional extension. The [browser lab](../../cases/trust/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) cannot read the file from the OSF, so it shows the reproduction as the course pipeline computed it, beside its code. | 45 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd#adjustment), the adjustment sets, and in Level 3 [countries and rounds](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd#fe) and [standard errors](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd#errors) | The four sets of controls that the curve keeps and what each holds constant; then the fixed-effects structures and the rules of inference that the menu offers, with the reason for each one that it leaves off the curve. | 30 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd), [The linear model](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-ols) | A regression in its plainest form, the straight line with noise of which every later model is a variation. | 40 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd), from [Clustered standard errors](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-pooled) to [Standard errors with few clusters](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-inference) | Clustered standard errors and what they correct; the two fixed-effects designs; and standard errors with few clusters, with the CR2 correction and its Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. | 80 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd), [Within and between](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-re) and [Multilevel models](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-multilevel) | Random effects, why they assume that the country departures are uncorrelated with the predictor, and the within–between model that separates the two comparisons; then multilevel models fitted to respondents, the design that the OA used. | 60 minutes |
| [Weights](../../companion/weighting.qmd#sec-trust), the section on this case | The design, post-stratification and population weights of the ESS in a regression on respondents, what each makes the estimate describe, the coefficient as an average of one slope per country, and which uses of the weights stay on the curve. | 45 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd#inference), inference with 16 countries | The reference specification under five rules of inference, why the respondents of one country are not independent pieces of evidence, and the CR2 correction that checks the clustered test. | 25 minutes |

**Shortcuts.** If you have fitted regressions with controls before, skip the linear model. If multilevel models are familiar, read only the sections on standard errors with few clusters and on within and between, which carry the arguments that the later cases use.

**By the end of the stage** you have reproduced *t* = 46.625 yourself and can say why the same specification gives 0.174 on the course extract, and you can say for the reference specification what changes, and what does not, when its country-round fixed effects become random intercepts, when it is weighted, and when its errors are clustered by country rather than treated as independent. The exercises "The model of the paper on the course data" and "The uncertainty of the estimate" in the section "Going further" of your report put each of those comparisons in numbers.
